subjects.name: A Letter from a Christian in 2012

summary: Child psychologist James Dobson built Focus on the Family into a US evangelical radio and lobbying empire that promoted corporal punishment of children and ran the Love Won Out gay conversion therapy conferences.

evidence.note: Dobson's birth and Louisiana origins introduced; childhood beatings by his mother described
first book Dare to Discipline published in 1970, start of his public career
couple charged with child abuse after following Dobson's spanking advice
entry into politics via Carter family conference, later Reagan-era panels and the FRC
radio empire, magazines, Adventures in Odyssey and the Colorado Springs headquarters
Dobson monetises Ted Bundy's final interview tapes and keeps much of the money
2008 anonymous letter imagining America in 2012 under Obama, read at length
Love Won Out ex-gay traveling conference and its claim that homosexuality is preventable
John Paulk's life, gay bar scandal, departure and 2013 apology
Dobson leaves in 2009 and Love Won Out is sold to Exodus; later downsizing
Pence at the 2017 anniversary and current anti-trans content carry the story to release

notes: Dobson was alive when this aired (2020); he died in 2025, so covered_span ends at the 2020 release per the lifetime rule. Main span runs from Dare to Discipline (1970) to his 2009 exit. Conversion therapy tagged as quackery-pseudoscience. Garrison Davis hosts; Robert Evans appears as guest. Family Research Council kept as a keyword to stay within five subjects.
